messages:
samir: heads up — customer acct-987 opened an escalation. their streaming request dropped after ~14s, client saw EOF and retries, but billing shows full token consumption. request_id=req_0a9f3c. logs attached below. :frowning:

samir: here's the gateway trace we have:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:14.123Z gateway[gw-12]: accept conn from 10.4.5.6
2026-03-15T09:12:14.125Z gateway[gw-12]: proxy to runtime pool-3 req=req_0a9f3c
2026-03-15T09:12:28.341Z runtime[rt-7]: stream chunked send 1 (8KB) req=req_0a9f3c
2026-03-15T09:12:28.342Z runtime[rt-7]: write to client: write tcp 10.4.5.6:443->203.0.113.17:52123: write: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T09:12:28.343Z gateway[gw-12]: upstream error: broken pipe; classifying as 502 for now req=req_0a9f3c
```

samir: customer reproduced with curl and pasted this snippet from their client: "recv returned 0, connection closed by server". they claim they haven't received final chunk but were billed. they're asking for refund + fix.

jen-oncall: thanks Samir — can you paste the full request metadata (model, seq len, streaming flags) and the client code they used? also pinging @maria-billing for billing impact. :eyes:

samir: model=redwood-3b-stream, max_tokens=1024, stream=true. client command they ran: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -d @prompt.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream`

devon-eng: seeing the "write: connection reset by peer" makes me think client closed the socket mid-stream. our infra currently increments 5xx if gateway sees upstream send error. that can misattribute a client-side disconnect as a server 5xx. we should decide what to report to billing.

maria-billing: if it's a client-initiated close we shouldn't bill for the unreceived tokens. we need exact token accounting per-segment and the request_id + account to correlate. Samir can you confirm account id and full request id?

samir: account=acct-987, full req id=req_0a9f3c. attaching the access log line from our edge: `203.0.113.17 - - [15/Mar/2026:09:12:14 +0000] \"POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\" 502 512 \"-\" \"curl/7.88.1\" req_id=req_0a9f3c`

ops-bot: deploy 2143584000 finished; no runtime restarts in last 24h. (automated check) :white_check_mark:

devon-eng: can we reproduce locally? try running a flaky-network sim: `tc qdisc` to add packet loss and force client to drop after 14s. also try `--no-buffer` curl to avoid local buffering.

samir: repro attempt: i ran curl with `--limit-rate 50k` and forced client close after 14s; runtime streamed 3 chunks and then gateway logged write error and we marked 502. reproduced.

jen-oncall: OK this looks like a "client heartbeat / silent close" race. two fixes: (1) change metrics/classification so ECONNRESET from downstream is not automatically a 5xx for billing purposes, and (2) server-side precaution: include a short finalization heartbeat chunk every 5s so we can detect client liveness earlier. tagging eng work. :hammer_and_wrench:

maria-billing: +1 on changing metric classification. until fixed we should create a case-by-case refund path. i'll need a list of affected request_ids this incident. Samir can you run a query for acct-987: `select * from request_events where account_id='acct-987' and status_code=502 and ts > '2026-03-15T08:00:00Z'` and paste results.

samir: pasted results: `req_0a9f3c, req_0a9f8d, req_0a9fef` (all within 09:10–09:20 window). all show upstream write errors in gateway logs.

devon-eng: note — our runtime's chunk flush logic currently flushes partial tokens as they become available. when the client disconnects mid-chunk we still have billed tokens because we accounted generation at runtime before transport success. that accounting model means we need transport confirmation before final billing. changing that is non-trivial (affects many metrics).

jen-oncall: short-term mitigation plan:
- bump telemetry: emit `client_disconnect=true` event when we get downstream ECONNRESET and mark in logs (non-billing).
- ops: add a small guard that if runtime sees downstream reset within 2s of sending last chunk, mark as "client disconnect suspected" and exclude from auto-charge pipeline.
- eng: backlog a robust solution to reconcile token accounting with transport ack.

maria-billing: i can do manual refunds for those three reqs once samir confirms. will open refunds and note reasoning.

devon-eng: follow-up technical note for records: sample reproduction command i used: ```bash
PROMPT='{"input":"repeat a 30s streaming poem"}'
curl -v -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d \"$PROMPT\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream | sed -n '1,50p' &
# sleep 14; kill $! # simulate client close
```

samir: i've run the query and submitted refund ticket #RF-4521 for acct-987. customer informed. i'll attach logs and the three req ids to the ticket.

jen-oncall: creating a short-lived alarm to surface upstream write errors count spike: `alert if gateway.upstream_write_errors > 5 within 5m` so SRE can react faster. i've added a task in eng oncall board to patch metric classification.

ops-bot: incident-note created: \"streaming-client-eof-heartbeat-race\" — priority P2.

samir: customer confirmed refund accepted, will monitor for recurrence. leaving this thread open for the eng team to track the longer-term accounting change. thanks all. :raised_hands:
